title: Automated prediction of phosphorus concentration in soils using reflectance spectroscopy
author: Rivadeneira-Bolaños, Nope-Rodríguez, et al.

steps.title: Prepare soil‑fertilizer mixtures
steps.instruction: Using air‑dried acidic clay soil from Santander de Quilichao and diammonium phosphate (P2O5) fertilizer, create a series of mixtures where the fertilizer proportion is reduced proportionally from 100 % (sample 1) to 0 % (sample 152) following the procedure of F. Rivadeneira.

substeps.instruction: Obtain air‑dried acidic clay soil characteristic of the region.

Mix soil and fertilizer in a series of ratios, starting with 100 % fertilizer (sample 1) and ending with soil only (sample 152), reducing the fertilizer proportion proportionally for each intermediate sample.

steps.title: Measure total phosphorus concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the total phosphorus (P‑Total) in each prepared mixture using the standardized chemical determination methods for soils, recording results for the 12 mixtures listed in Table 2.

substeps.instruction: Apply the standard soil chemical analysis protocol to each of the 12 prepared samples.
Measure P‑Total (mg kg⁻¹) for each sample.
Document the concentrations as shown in Table 2 (e.g., 12.571 mg kg⁻¹ for sample 1, 0.001 mg kg⁻¹ for the method detection limit, etc.).

steps.title: Reduce spectral data via PCA
steps.instruction: Load the 152 reflectance spectra (each containing 3501 wavelength points) and apply Principal Component Analysis to compress each spectrum to two principal component scores.

substeps.instruction: Import the 152 spectra with 3501 wavelengths per spectrum into the analysis environment.
Perform PCA on the full dataset.
Retain the first two principal components, resulting in a dataset of 152 samples with 2 values each.

steps.title: Train and validate ML models
steps.instruction: Using MATLAB R2022a, train two machine‑learning algorithms on the PCA‑reduced data, employing an 80 %/20 % train‑test split and 10‑fold cross‑validation for robust evaluation.

substeps.instruction: Implement the two chosen algorithms in MATLAB R2022a.
Randomly allocate 80 % of the 152 samples to a training set and the remaining 20 % to a test set.
Within the training set, create 10 folds and perform cross‑validation to tune and assess model performance.
After training, evaluate the final models on the independent test set.

description: We present a method based on the training and validation of two machine learning algorithms. To achieve optimal performance, these algorithms require high-quality data with relevant information, and their implementation was carried out in MATLAB R2022a. In the previous section, we explained the process of obtaining, preprocessing, and reducing the dimensionality of the data. Initially, we had 152 spectra, each with 3501 wavelengths. Using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), we reduced these data to 152 samples with only 2 points each. This significant reduction in dimensionality not only preserves the essential information but also considerably decreases computational cost. From there, we implemented two learning algorithms. We trained each algorithm using 80% of the data for training and the remaining 20% for testing. Additionally, we created training sets through 10-fold cross-validation, thus ensuring a more robust and reliable evaluation of the models [20].
